subject: FinPay: P99 latency spike during autoscaler provisioning - immediate attention
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finpay.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@finpay.com
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production P99 spike during scale-up (FinPay)

Hannah,

We observed a significant P99 latency regression in production at 08:57 PDT during a normal traffic surge. Baseline p99 for our text-generation route is usually ~320ms; during the incident we saw sustained p99s of 3.2s for ~12 minutes and multiple 5-6s outliers. Error rate remained low (~0.1%) but throughput dropped as clients retried. This coincided with an autoscaler event where additional GPU workers were provisioned.

Attached is a Grafana snapshot and a short timeline from our side. Can you confirm whether this is related to new instance startup / model load time on Redwood's hosted pool? FinPay is on a performance SLA and this hit a few live payments flows — we need an explanation and short-term mitigation.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Engineering, FinPay
liam.oconnor@finpay.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finpay.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production P99 spike during scale-up (FinPay)

We investigated the traces and infra telemetry for the 08:55–09:10 window. Short summary:

What we saw:
- Autoscaler requested +4 GPU workers (A100 equiv) starting at 08:53:02.
- New instances passed health checks and became routable ~2:40–3:10 minutes after provisioning.
- First routed requests to new workers showed high token-level latency (p99 token generation ~1200ms) for the first ~20–30 requests.
- Significant KV cache miss rate on first requests for those workers (model context & key-value cache cold).

Root cause hypothesis: the latency spike is primarily a "provisioning + model-warmup" effect. When new workers were marked as healthy we started routing production traffic to them before their KV cache was populated, which amplified p99s across the route as the routing balanced across both warm and cold workers.

Evidence attached: aggregated startup latency timeline and sample stack traces (see service_logs.zip).

Short-term mitigations we propose (can be applied within 1–2 hours):
1) Change routing policy for FinPay route to prefer warm workers during scale events (sticky-routing / min-uptime threshold).
2) Enable small pre-warm pool for this customer (1–2 kept-warm workers) to handle initial surges.
3) Reduce per-worker max concurrency during initial 5 minutes after provisioning to avoid compounding cache misses.

Longer-term fixes:
- Improve model population parallelism on startup and warm cache prefetch for typical request patterns.
- Add autoscaler hook to delay routing until KV cache hit-rate reaches threshold.

Attaching: service_logs.zip (zip, 8MB) — includes startup traces, profiler samples, and KV-cache metrics.

— Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finpay.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Exec summary & proposed action (FinPay autoscale latency event)

Team —

Executive summary for leadership:
- Impact: A production autoscaler event for FinPay on 2026-10-05 led to routing to newly provisioned workers before their model KV caches reached steady state. Observed: ~12 minutes of elevated p99 (median p99 ~3.2s, peaking 5–6s) affecting ~7% of FinPay requests during the window. Error rate did not materially increase.
- Business impact: FinPay flagged payment flow retries; they have requested an SLA credit estimate and a short-term mitigation within the next 24 hours.

Actions taken so far:
- Karthik analyzed startup telemetry and attached logs; short-term mitigations proposed (routing policy + pre-warm).
- CS contacted FinPay and confirmed timeline + trace uploads.

Proposed immediate actions (requesting approval to proceed):
1) Apply routing policy override for FinPay to prefer warm workers for 48 hours (rollback safe). Expected RTO: ~1 hour to deploy config.
2) Allocate 1 dedicated pre-warm worker for FinPay for 7 days while we implement more robust warmup hooks (cost impact minimal; suggest offsetting with account credits).
3) Start a root-cause ticket for longer-term engineering work: startup parallelization & autoscaler readiness gating.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: pre-warm allocation increases cost; mitigate with temporary account credit and review after 7 days.
- Risk: routing policy changes may slightly reduce burst capacity; we will monitor and adjust autoscaler thresholds.

Please reply with approval for (1) + (2) so we can execute. I propose we offer FinPay a one-month pro-rated credit equivalent to the impacted usage as a customer-goodwill gesture; Marissa, can you coordinate?

— Hannah Schmitt
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

CC: Grace O'Connor (Head of Customer Success)
